scope: source-grounded authoring cards; not runtime verification

rooms.question: How far can one branching instruction carry a structure?
rooms.ontology: Recursion calls a construction on smaller or later parts, with a stopping condition; a tree stores parent-child relations.
rooms.action: Follow one thick branch into its smaller descendants, then find a second branch that repeats the relationship without matching every dimension.
rooms.observable: Box-like limbs differ in widths and orientations while inheriting a repeated branching structure.
rooms.mechanism: generate_branches chooses seeded random sizes and directions, builds children at branch endpoints and recurses with current_depth+1 until max_depth.
rooms.limit: Finite depth and random variation make this an approximation with family resemblance, not an infinite exact self-copy. A branching shape is not evidence of biological growth.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Reveal one generation at a time and preserve the random seed so only recursion depth changes.
rooms.cautions: Source read only; actual museum runtime, reachability, controls and learner understanding remain unverified. UI sliders are2D; no promised VR branch dragging.

rooms.question: Can repeated removal produce more pieces while leaving less material?
rooms.ontology: The middle-third construction replaces each interval with its two outer thirds. Count and total length move in different directions.
rooms.action: Watch one subdivision and count the descendants of a bar; compare the gap with either surviving third.
rooms.observable: Each retained segment produces two shorter ones, while the deleted middle separates them.
rooms.mechanism: perform_iteration finds a bar length, creates length/3 children displaced ±length/3, while retaining the earlier displayed rows; timed grow mode uses physical bars, while instant mode freezes rows.
rooms.limit: A finite set of thick bars is not the infinite Cantor set. Falling or displaced bodies are consequences of this exhibit and must be distinguished from the mathematical interval.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Retain deleted middles as ghost or scar readouts so visitors can compare what the rule removes with what it keeps.
rooms.cautions: Source read only; actual museum runtime, reachability, controls and learner understanding remain unverified.

rooms.question: Can a repeated cut increase visible intricacy while reducing volume?
rooms.ontology: Subdivision divides a cube into27 equal parts; the Menger rule retains20 by removing the centre and face-centred parts.
rooms.action: Inspect an opening through the sponge, then look for the same pattern of openings at a smaller scale.
rooms.observable: Repeated square tunnels and smaller retained cubes occupy the original envelope.
rooms.mechanism: subdivide_cube_menger loops3×3×3 offsets, skips cells with at least two zero indices, scales children by1/3 and replaces the parent.
rooms.limit: The displayed finite stages retain positive volume and finite detail. Mathematical limit claims need reasoning beyond what a headset can resolve.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Keep the removed seven parts beside one retained block for one stage, and let visitors reconstruct the cut.

sources.fact: perform_iteration and subdivide_cube_menger: local subtree only,20 retained subcubes.

rooms.cautions: Source read only; actual museum runtime, reachability, controls and learner understanding remain unverified. No claim of user-operated subdivision or traversable tunnels; small scene scale matters.

rooms.question: Which part of a growing pattern comes from addition, and which part comes from its drawing?
rooms.ontology: A recurrence constructs each number from earlier values; an encoding determines how those numbers occupy space.
rooms.action: Read three consecutive labelled values and check whether the last equals the earlier two; compare that arithmetic with the tower heights.
rooms.observable: The numbers follow1,1,2,3,5…; tower heights grow more slowly than the numbers.
rooms.mechanism: generate_fibonacci_sequence adds the previous two values; visualize_number_sequence uses log(number)*0.5+0.5 for tower height and highlights successive indices.
rooms.limit: Tower proportions are logarithmic, so height ratios cannot be read as Fibonacci ratios. A recurrence does not prove all natural growth follows the golden ratio.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Place linear and logarithmic encodings beside the same numbered sequence, then invent a different starting pair.
rooms.cautions: Source read only; actual museum runtime, reachability, controls and learner understanding remain unverified.

rooms.question: What makes two very different objects examples of recursion?
rooms.ontology: A recursive explanation names what is repeated, how a child relates to its parent, and why the construction stops.
rooms.action: Choose a Cantor segment and a tree branch. Explain one next step for each before looking at their smaller descendants.
rooms.observable: The interval construction deletes a middle third; the tree adds branches, yet each repeats a relation at another level.
rooms.mechanism: Cantor uses two children of length/3; recursive_tree calls generate_branches with an increased depth and depth-scaled randomly sized limbs.
rooms.limit: Recursion alone does not guarantee exact self-similarity or the same dimension. Sharing a programming technique does not erase the different meanings of removal and branching.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Exchange a rule between the pair: design a branching interval or a tree that withholds its central branch, and predict what the exchange changes.
rooms.cautions: Source read only; actual museum runtime, reachability, controls and learner understanding remain unverified. Uses two earlier artifacts in a new comparative role; remaining synthesis displays stay available without all becoming primary.

rooms.question: How can a line visit a region without becoming a sheet?
rooms.ontology: A finite curve is an ordered path; recursive rules can make progressively finer paths visit a grid more densely.
rooms.action: Follow a stretch on one panel, then compare the way another panel turns and returns through its area.
rooms.observable: Three differently organised traces share a framed region but distribute their turns differently.
rooms.mechanism: Gallery rewrites Hilbert,Peano and Moore grammars for finite iterations, interprets F as movement and ± as90° turns, and draws the paths into a texture.
rooms.limit: Finite images have gaps and pixel thickness. A space-filling limit is not proved by a dense drawing, and these panels are not physical paths to walk.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Compare multiple depths of one grammar with equal framing and line width before comparing separate grammars.
